title: Unramified diagonal tested on the automorphism space of a smooth atlas
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$, and $p:P\to\mathcal X$ a smooth surjective morphism with $P$ a scheme. Let $G_p$ denote the algebraic space representing $T\mapsto\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal X(T)}(p|_T)$ on $P$-schemes. Then $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ is unramified if and only if $G_p\to P$ is unramified. An algebraic stack here is a stack in groupoids on schemes over $S$ with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Fibred groupoids, stacks, representability and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Smoothness and surjectivity of a representable map are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts, using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and ordinary surjectivity on points. Unramifiedness for morphisms of algebraic spaces is tested etale locally on source and target using [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Unramifiedness of the representable diagonal is tested after every scheme base change using this algebraic-space convention.

source.place: Tag 0CL0 (lemma-diagonal-diagonal), part (4), for the structure morphism to S, with Tag 050Q (lemma-inertia) identifying atlas pullback of inertia with G_p; smooth-local descent of representable unramifiedness is the property listed in stacks-properties.tex, section-properties-morphisms, using spaces-descent.tex Tag 042A (lemma-descending-property-unramified).

proof.text: First identify the diagonal base changes. For an $S$-scheme $T$ and objects $a,b\in\mathcal X(T)$, the base change of $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}$ along $(a,b):T\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ represents $\operatorname{Isom}_T(a,b)$. Indeed its objects over $T'\to T$ are triples $(z,\alpha:z\xrightarrow{\sim}a_{T'},\beta:z\xrightarrow{\sim}b_{T'})$; send this to $\beta\alpha^{-1}$. The inverse sends $\phi:a_{T'}\xrightarrow{\sim}b_{T'}$ to $(a_{T'},1,\phi)$, and $\alpha$ gives the unique compatible isomorphism to that triple. These operations commute with pullback. In particular, take $T=P$ and $a=b=p$ to obtain $G_p$. If the diagonal is unramified, its scheme base change $G_p\to P$ is unramified by the testing convention in the statement. This proves the forward implication.

source.place: Tag 0CL0 (lemma-diagonal-diagonal), proof of (4), diagonal base-change square; Tag 050Q (lemma-inertia), automorphism square.

proof.text: For the converse assume $G_p\to P$ unramified. Fix an arbitrary $S$-scheme $T$ and $a,b\in\mathcal X(T)$. Put $I=\operatorname{Isom}_T(a,b)$ and $H=\operatorname{Aut}_T(b)$. The Isom local-finite-type theorem says that both are algebraic spaces locally of finite type over $T$, and that $H$ is a group algebraic space with composition as multiplication. These assertions apply to $a,b$ and to $b,b$ without any finite type hypothesis on $T$ or $\mathcal X$.

source.place: Tag 04XR (lemma-isom-locally-finite-type), also used in the proof of Tag 050Q (lemma-inertia).

proof.text: Form the 2-fibre product $W=T\times_{b,\mathcal X,p}P$. Its objects on a test scheme $V$ are $(t:V\to T,v:V\to P,\theta:b_t\xrightarrow{\sim}p_v)$. The pullback of the diagonal along $(b,p):T\times_S P\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ is equivalent to $W$: as in step 1, send $(z,\alpha:z\xrightarrow{\sim}b_t,\beta:z\xrightarrow{\sim}p_v)$ to $\theta=\beta\alpha^{-1}$, with inverse $(b_t,1,\theta)$. These operations preserve compatible arrows, pullbacks and both projections. Thus $W$ is an algebraic space by representability of the diagonal. Its projection $q:W\to T$ is smooth and surjective by base change of the atlas. The current chartwise calculus uses field-extension local lifting for surjectivity: for every $t:\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$, the atlas supplies, after $K\hookrightarrow L$, a lift $v:\operatorname{Spec}L\to P$ and an isomorphism $b_{t_L}\simeq p_v$. This is precisely a point of $W$ above $t_L$. Its statement equates this condition, for a representable map, with surjectivity on every scheme base change and surjective etale scheme chart. Thus its surjectivity convention agrees with the one required for descent. The same calculus makes $q$ flat and locally of finite presentation. Hence $q$ has exactly the hypotheses of the representable-unramified descent theorem. Write $u:W\to P$ for the other projection.

source.place: Section 04XB (section-properties-morphisms), base change of representable smooth surjections; Tag 04XD (lemma-check-property-covering).

proof.text:
The tautological isomorphism on $W$ gives
$$W\times_T H\ \simeq\ W\times_P G_p.$$
Here is the identification on each scheme $V\to W$: its data include $t:V\to T$, $v:V\to P$ and $\theta:b_t\xrightarrow{\sim}p_v$. Send $h\in\operatorname{Aut}(b_t)$ to $\theta h\theta^{-1}\in\operatorname{Aut}(p_v)$, with inverse $g\mapsto\theta^{-1}g\theta$. The two composites are identities. For every $f:V\prime\to V$, pullback preserves composition and inverses, so $f^*(\theta h\theta^{-1})=(f^*\theta)(f^*h)(f^*\theta)^{-1}$; the inverse formula has the same compatibility. They therefore define inverse maps of the algebraic spaces over $W$. No global lift of $b$ to $P$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 050Q (lemma-inertia), identification of atlas pullback with automorphisms; conjugation on the defining 2-fibre product.

proof.text: Base-change stability of unramified algebraic-space morphisms makes $W\times_P G_p\to W$ unramified. Step 4 therefore makes $W\times_T H\to W$ unramified. Apply representable-unramified descent to $H\to T$ and $q:W\to T$: $H$ and $T$ are algebraic spaces, $H\to T$ is representable by algebraic spaces, and step 3 supplies the surjective flat locally finitely presented cover. It follows that $H\to T$ is unramified.

Composition gives an action $H\times_T I\to I$, $(g,\phi)\mapsto g\phi$. Associativity and the identity law are those in the groupoid $\mathcal X(V)$ for each scheme $V\to T$. The map
$$H\times_T I\longrightarrow I\times_T I,\qquad(g,\phi)\longmapsto(g\phi,\phi)$$
has inverse $(\psi,\phi)\mapsto(\psi\phi^{-1},\phi)$. Both composites are identities on all test schemes and the formulas respect pullback, so these are inverse morphisms of algebraic spaces. Thus $I$ is a pseudo $H$-torsor. This uses neither nonempty fibres nor a cover on which $a$ and $b$ are isomorphic.

source.place: Tag 04YP (lemma-isom-pseudo-torsor-aut), composition action; the same action in Tag 0CPK (lemma-isom-pseudo-torsor-aut-over-space).

proof.text: Apply the unramified pseudo-torsor lemma with base $B=T$, group $H$ and pseudo torsor $I$. Step 2 supplies local finite type for both $H$ and $I$, step 5 supplies unramifiedness of $H\to T$, and step 6 supplies the pseudo-torsor isomorphism. Hence $I\to T$ is unramified. Since $T,a,b$ were arbitrary, step 1 identifies every scheme base change of $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}$ with such a map $I\to T$. By the representable-diagonal testing convention, the diagonal is unramified, proving the converse.
